nodes.bio: Visionary industrial designer and founder of Dave Nutting Associates. He provided the core product concepts, cabinet layouts, and baseline game direction for historic titles like Gun Fight, Sea Wolf, Gorf, and Wizard of Wor.
Foundational electronics engineer who pioneered the 'Bally Brain' motherboard and designed the 3-chip custom AMI silicon family, creating the 'magic memory' blitter circuit.
Lead software architect who engineered the Professional Arcade system ROM (HVGSYS), Bally BASIC, and programmed the iconic multi-mission arcade hit Gorf.
Brilliant hacker and architect of the TERSE threaded language environment. He famously left DNA for Stern Electronics to build their video division and create Berzerk.
Key assembly programmer recruited out of UW-Milwaukee who worked side-by-side with Fenton and Frederiksen to write code directly hitting the custom Z80 system routines.
Essential early retail game programmer at DNA. He wrote Panzer Attack and Red Baron, co-authored Football, and authored the 'Perspective Box' video art demo.
Workhorse game designer who specialized in home consumer cartridges. He co-authored Football and later formed Action Graphics with Nutting's direct support.
Custom silicon engineer at DNA who helped lay out the logic circuits for the three custom AMI chips alongside Jeff Frederiksen.
Printed circuit board layout specialist who managed the physical mainboard routing for the home console and arcade board stacks.
DNA hardware engineering manager who led the add-on computer systems. He later recruited McNeil to Stern to design the arcade hardware for Berzerk.
American Microsystems Inc. (AMI) engineer who worked directly with Frederiksen to translate DNA's logic schematics into physical five-micrometer silicon.
Dave Nutting's brother and founder of Nutting Associates in California, the company that originally manufactured Nutting's and Nolan Bushnell's Computer Space.
Early software programmer at Dave Nutting Associates who authored the console's built-in multi-player strategy game Checkmate.
Pioneering external developer who reverse-engineered the console. He provided the Cursor Group with its machine language entry points and co-founded Spectre Systems.
Astrocade archivist and founder of the Cursor Group user collective who published Brett Bilbrey's early machine language memory maps and programming tutorials.
Co-founder of Spectre Systems who helped publish the third-party commercial cartridges Treasure Cove and the legendary ultra-rare ICBM Attack.
Co-founder of Spectre Systems who served as a key technical developer during the creation of the custom Spectre Handle peripheral joystick.
Milwaukee Coin Industries partner and employee photographed standing with David Nutting beside the Red Baron electromechanical flyer in 1971.
Early MCI coin-op route and design contemporary photographed standing beside the Red Baron arcade cabinet in 1971.
Co-founder and editor of Electronic Games magazine who interviewed Bob Ogdon for the landmark May 1982 'Inside Gaming' studio feature profile.
Bob Ogdon's spouse who explicitly introduced him to Dave Nutting, leading to his exploratory recruitment trip to Chicago and hiring at DNA.
Action Graphics game designer whose debut fantasy program Quest for the Orb for the Astro Arcade was supervised directly by Bob Ogdon.
Tech journalist who authored the September 1983 JoyStik feature article 'Astrocade's Underground,' documenting the cottage homebrew expansion industry.
Professional musician and founder of Wavemakers. He developed 18 software tapes for the BASIC cartridge, including an interactive guitar tuning course.
Founder of the third-party development house Tiny Arcade, which published the unique multi-screen scrolling space game Omega Valley.
Michigan-based audio expert who mastered the 3-channel sound chip. He published multiple music utilities and composed the soundtrack for Treasure Cove.
Founder of 'The Bit Fiddlers' development house and creator of the highly celebrated Machine Language Manager (MLM) utility cartridge.
Astrocade developer and data archivist who compiled the monumental 114-page semi-annual Sourcebook catalog of every known program and expansion module.
The historic, central archivist of the platform who published the monthly ARCADIAN user group newsletter, single-handedly keeping the technical community alive.
Co-founder of ABC Hobbycraft, a premier midwestern retail dealer of Astrocade hardware, memory components, and cassette-based third-party software tapes.
